```{r setup}
#| include: false
suppressMessages({
  library(baeconstrat)
  library(ggplot2)
})
root <- normalizePath("..")
rd <- function(f) readRDS(file.path(root, "output", f))
CFG <- local({
  old <- setwd(root); on.exit(setwd(old))
  e <- new.env(); sys.source("analysis/00_config.R", envir = e); e$CFG
})
P  <- rd("panels.rds");   S1 <- rd("stage1.rds"); S2 <- rd("stage2.rds")
N  <- rd("ngfb.rds");     SC <- rd("scenarios.rds")
O  <- rd("optimise.rds"); BT <- rd("backtest.rds"); MC <- rd("model_checks.rds")

## formatting ---------------------------------------------------------------
pct  <- function(x, d = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f%%"), 100 * x)
spct <- function(x, d = 1) sprintf(paste0("%+.", d, "f%%"), 100 * x)
pp   <- function(x, d = 1) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f pp"), 100 * abs(x))
nb <- "\u00a0"                                      # keep numbers and units together
bps  <- function(x, d = 0) { v <- round(1e4 * x, d); v[v == 0] <- 0; sprintf(paste0("%+.", d, "f", nb, "bps"), v) }
ubps <- function(x, d = 0) sprintf(paste0("%.", d, "f", nb, "bps"), 1e4 * abs(x))
num  <- function(x, d = 1) formatC(x, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ",")
rbn  <- function(x, d = 0) paste0("R", formatC(x / 1e6, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ","), nb, "bn")
srbn <- function(x, d = 1) { v <- round(x / 1e6, d); v[v == 0] <- 0
  paste0(ifelse(v < 0, "-R", "+R"), formatC(abs(v), format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ","), nb, "bn") }
urbn <- function(x, d = 1) paste0("R", formatC(abs(x) / 1e6, format = "f", digits = d, big.mark = ","), nb, "bn")
srm  <- function(x) { v <- round(x / 1e3); v[v == 0] <- 0
  paste0(ifelse(v < 0, "-R", "+R"), formatC(abs(v), format = "d", big.mark = ","), nb, "m") }
urm  <- function(x) paste0("R", formatC(round(abs(x) / 1e3), format = "d", big.mark = ","), nb, "m")
qlab <- function(d) paste0(format(as.Date(d), "%Y"), "Q", (as.integer(format(as.Date(d), "%m")) - 1) %/% 3 + 1)
## a value that rounds to zero is printed without a sign ("-0.0" becomes "0.0")
nz <- function(x) gsub("(?<![0-9.])-(0(?:\\.0+)?)(?![0-9.])", "\\1", x, perl = TRUE)
twin <- function(df, title = "Table view", digits = 2) {
  cat('\n::: {.callout-note collapse="true" appearance="simple"}\n## ', title, '\n\n', sep = "")
  cat(nz(knitr::kable(df, format = "pipe", digits = digits, row.names = FALSE)), sep = "\n")
  cat("\n:::\n")
}
kt <- function(df, digits = 2, ...) { k <- knitr::kable(df, digits = digits, row.names = FALSE, ...); k[] <- nz(k); k }

## palette and theme (validated with the dataviz validator: adjacent CVD and
## normal-vision gates pass; light slots carry legends and table twins) -------
pal <- viz_palette(); ink <- pal$ink
ent_col <- pal$entity
sc_col <- pal$scenario
sc_short <- c(baseline = "Baseline", upside = "Upside", downside = "Downside", downside_cuts = "Downside with cuts")
sc_long <- scenario_labels()
plab <- c(mortgages_res = "Home loans", mortgages_com = "Commercial mortgages", vaf = "VAF",
              cards = "Cards", personal_other = "Personal loans", corp_all = "Corporate loans",
              nmd = "Non-maturity deposits", beh_term = "Term deposits")
rlab <- c(contraction = "Contraction", hiking = "Hiking", easing = "Easing", neutral = "Neutral")
div_lo <- "#e34948"; div_mid <- "#f0efec"; div_hi <- "#2a78d6"
seq_ramp <- c("#cde2fb", "#86b6ef", "#3987e5", "#1c5cab", "#0d366b")
theme_set(theme_ngfb(12.5))

## key objects ---------------------------------------------------------------
res <- SC$results; scen <- names(res)
guard(identical(scen, c("baseline", "upside", "downside")), "the report is written for three scenarios")
allr <- c(res, SC$variants)
date0 <- CFG$date0
sumtab <- do.call(rbind, lapply(names(allr), function(k) data.frame(
  scenario = k, ngfb = allr[[k]]$ngfb$summary$roe, ngfb_nohedge = allr[[k]]$ngfb_unhedged$summary$roe,
  sector = allr[[k]]$sector$summary$roe, ni = allr[[k]]$ngfb$summary$net_income,
  ni_nohedge = allr[[k]]$ngfb_unhedged$summary$net_income, sector_ni = allr[[k]]$sector$summary$net_income,
  nim = allr[[k]]$ngfb$summary$nim, clr = allr[[k]]$ngfb$summary$clr, cet1_min = allr[[k]]$ngfb$summary$cet1_min,
  lcr_min = allr[[k]]$ngfb$summary$lcr_min, sector_nim = allr[[k]]$sector$summary$nim,
  sector_clr = allr[[k]]$sector$summary$clr)))
rownames(sumtab) <- sumtab$scenario
guard(all(abs(sumtab[scen, "ngfb"] - O$status_quo[scen]) < 1e-12), "scenario and optimiser outputs disagree on NGFB's ROE")
base <- sumtab["baseline", ]
yrs <- CFG$horizon / 4
bal <- N$balance; ta0 <- attr(bal, "size")
sec_ta0 <- P$gp$total_assets[P$gp$entity == "Sector" & P$gp$date == date0]
guard(abs(sum(bal$balance[bal$side == "asset"]) / ta0 - 1) < 1e-8, "NGFB size attribute disagrees with its balance sheet")
sens <- SC$sensitivities; rownames(sens) <- sens$shock
snh <- SC$sensitivities_nohedge; rownames(snh) <- snh$shock
att <- SC$attribution
att_r <- function(s, e = "NGFB", ch = "total", m = "roe") att[att$scenario == s & att$entity == e & att$metric == m, ch]
mv <- O$moves; rg <- O$regret
posD <- rg$positions["downside", ]; posU <- rg$positions["upside", ]
hedge_ratio0 <- SC$hedge0$notional / N$nmd0
guard(abs(hedge_ratio0 - ngfb_canonical()$hedge_ratio) < 1e-9, "hedge is not at the canonical ratio")
bp1 <- 1e-4 * O$m_ni[["baseline"]] / yrs            # net income a year per bp of ROE (R'000)
mr <- SC$model_risk; rownames(mr) <- mr$scenario
wc <- SC$what_changed

## the call-deposit outlier neutralised in the calibration window
imp_dates <- function(s) {
  m <- regmatches(s$impulses, regexpr("[0-9]{6}$", s$impulses))
  if (!length(m)) return(as.Date(character(0)))
  quarter_end(as.Date(paste0(m, "01"), "%Y%m%d"))
}
cc_out <- imp_dates(S1$sats$c_call); cc_out <- cc_out[cc_out %in% N$calibration$window]
guard(length(cc_out) == 1, "expected one flagged call-deposit quarter in the calibration window")
cc_val <- P$spnl$c_call[P$spnl$date == cc_out]

## every qualitative claim in the text is checked here --------------------------
## scenarios
guard(base$ngfb < base$sector && base$ngfb_nohedge < base$ngfb && base$clr > base$sector_clr,
      "hedge-carry paragraph: NGFB below the sector, the hedge adds in the baseline, higher credit losses")
guard(SC$hedge0$fixed0 > mean(res$baseline$scenario$float3m), "the hedge should carry positively in the baseline")
guard(att_r("upside") > 0 && att_r("upside", "Sector") < 0 && att_r("upside", "Sector", "pricing") < 0 &&
      att_r("upside", "NGFB", "pricing") > 0 && att_r("upside", "NGFB", "credit") > att_r("upside", "NGFB", "pricing"),
      "upside: NGFB gains (credit first, then pricing), the sector loses its endowment")
guard(att_r("downside") < 0 && att_r("downside", "NGFB", "pricing") < 0 && att_r("downside", "NGFB", "credit") < 0 &&
      abs(att_r("downside", "NGFB", "credit")) > abs(att_r("downside", "NGFB", "pricing")),
      "downside: NGFB loses through credit first and pricing second")
guard(att_r("downside", "Sector", "pricing") > 0 && att_r("downside", "Sector", "credit") < 0 &&
      abs(att_r("downside", "Sector")) < abs(att_r("downside")) / 4,
      "downside: the sector's endowment offsets its credit losses")
guard(att_r("downside_cuts", "NGFB", "pricing") > 0 && att_r("downside_cuts", "Sector", "pricing") < 0 &&
      att_r("downside_cuts") > att_r("downside") && att_r("downside_cuts", "Sector") < att_r("downside_cuts"),
      "downside with cuts: the hedge protects NGFB, the sector loses")
## sensitivities
guard(sens["repo_up_100", "total"] < 0 && snh["repo_up_100", "total"] > 0 && sens["repo_down_100", "total"] > 0,
      "hedged NGFB is liability-sensitive, unhedged asset-sensitive")
guard(sens["gdp_down_1", "total"] < 0 && sens["hpi_down_10", "total"] < 0 && sens["cpi_up_1", "total"] > 0,
      "growth, house-price and inflation signs")
guard(sens["unemp_up_2", "credit"] == 0 && abs(sens["unemp_up_2", "total"]) < 1e-3, "no unemployment channel")
guard(abs(sens["gdp_down_1", "credit"]) > abs(sens["repo_up_100", "total"]), "growth is the largest single exposure")
## positioning
guard(all(lengths(rg$binding) == 0), "a constraint binds; revise the text")
guard(posD[["hedge"]] < 0 && posD[["fund_savings"]] > 0 && posD[["fund_operational"]] > 0 &&
      posD[["into_cards"]] < 0 && posD[["into_personal"]] < 0, "downside positioning directions")
guard(posU[["hedge"]] > 0 && posU[["into_personal"]] > 0 && posU[["into_cards"]] > 0 &&
      posU[["fund_savings"]] < 0 && posU[["fund_operational"]] < 0, "upside positioning directions")
guard(max(abs(c(posD[1:9], posU[1:9]))) < 0.5, "balance-sheet tilts are described as small")
guard(rg$gain["downside", "downside"] > 0 && rg$gain["downside", "baseline"] < 0 && rg$gain["downside", "upside"] < 0 &&
      rg$gain["upside", "upside"] > 0 && rg$gain["upside", "baseline"] < 0 && rg$gain["upside", "downside"] < 0,
      "positioning: gain if right, cost if wrong")
guard(rg$gain["downside", "downside"] < abs(att_r("downside")) / 5, "positioning recovers a small part of the downside")
for (s in c("upside", "downside")) guard(max(abs(O$walk[[s]]$x - O$walk[[s]]$x_unc)) < 1e-4,
                                         "the %s positioning is not the unconstrained optimum", s)
xc <- O$cuts$x
guard(xc[["hedge"]] > 0 && xc[["into_cards"]] < 0 && xc[["into_personal"]] < 0, "downside-with-cuts positioning")
guard(sign(xc[["hedge"]]) != sign(posD[["hedge"]]) && sign(xc[["into_personal"]]) == sign(posD[["into_personal"]]),
      "the hedge flips with the policy response; unsecured lending does not")
## model checks
guard(MC$ardl11_better && MC$ic_level_better && !MC$convex_adopt, "model-check verdicts")
guard(setequal(MC$asym$target[MC$asym$adopt], c("c_current", "c_savings", "s_commercial", "s_cards")) &&
      !any(MC$vol_asym$adopt) && setequal(MC$kinks$target[MC$kinks$adopt], "g_cards"), "asymmetries adopted")
guard(MC$comb_all[["bma"]] > MC$comb_all[["comb"]] && MC$comb_all[["bma"]] > MC$comb_all[["best"]],
      "BIC model averaging beats the out-of-sample combination and the single best")
guard(MC$bounds$decision[MC$bounds$target == "c_current"] == "level relationship" &&
      MC$bounds$decision[MC$bounds$target == "c_savings"] == "no level relationship", "bounds-test claims")
guard(mr["upside", "convex"] < mr["upside", "core"] && abs(mr["downside", "convex"] - mr["downside", "core"]) < 0.002,
      "convex credit: smaller upside, unchanged downside")
guard(mr["baseline", "core"] - mr["baseline", "no_ic_credit"] > 0.01, "the credit intercept correction is material")
## what changed: the previous version's published baseline ROE (v0.3.0, 14 October 2026), the same with
## this version's models but the old swap proxy, and the core
roe_v3 <- 0.1487
## the previous version's published scenario ROEs (v0.4.0 and v0.5.0, both 21 October 2026)
roe_v4 <- c(baseline = 0.13313, upside = 0.14865, downside = 0.10753)
roe_v5 <- c(baseline = 0.13245, upside = 0.14813, downside = 0.10717)
guard(all(abs(sumtab[scen, "ngfb"] - roe_v5[scen]) < 5e-6), "the plan's ROE has moved since v0.5.0: revise What changed")
guard(all(vapply(scen, function(k) wc[[k]]$roe > sumtab[k, "ngfb"], TRUE)) && wc$baseline$roe > roe_v3 &&
      base$ngfb < roe_v3, "what-changed decomposition: models up, swap correction down, net down")
## stage 2 (unchanged from the previous version)
cgc <- S2$coef_groups
cgt <- function(e, p, k = "(Intercept)") cgc$t[cgc$entity == e & cgc$product == p & cgc$param == k]
cge <- function(e, p, k = "(Intercept)") cgc$est[cgc$entity == e & cgc$product == p & cgc$param == k]
guard(all(c(cgt("Challengers", "cards"), cgt("Challengers", "dep_retail"), cgt("Challengers", "nmd")) > 2.5) &&
      all(c(cge("Challengers", "cards"), cge("Challengers", "dep_retail"), cge("Challengers", "nmd")) > 10),
      "Challengers' drift claims")
guard(all(c(cgt("Big Four", "cards"), cgt("Big Four", "dep_retail"), cgt("Big Four", "mortgages_res")) < -2),
      "Big Four drift claims")
rsc <- N$regime_share
rsv <- function(e, p, r) rsc$ds_pp_yr[rsc$entity == e & rsc$product == p & rsc$regime == r]
guard(rsv("Big Four", "cards", "contraction") < 0 && rsv("Challengers", "cards", "contraction") > 0 &&
      rsv("NGFB", "cards", "contraction") > 0, "cards in contraction")
guard(rsv("Specialists", "nmd", "hiking") > max(rsv("NGFB", "nmd", "hiking"), rsv("Challengers", "nmd", "hiking")) &&
      rsv("NGFB", "nmd", "hiking") > 0 && rsv("Challengers", "nmd", "hiking") > 0 && rsv("Big Four", "nmd", "hiking") < 0,
      "NMD in hiking")
guard(N$calibration$wholesale_spread_raw < 0 && N$calibration$wholesale_spread > 0, "wholesale spread claims")
nir_gap <- SC$no_ic$sector$roe - base$sector
guard(nir_gap > 0.005, "the uncorrected NIR model should inflate the sector's ROE")
cz <- P$macro[P$macro$date >= as.Date("2025-03-31") & is.finite(P$macro$coinc_yy) & is.finite(P$macro$gdp_yy), ]
guard(nrow(cz) > 0 && mean(cz$coinc_yy < 0 & cz$gdp_yy > 0) >= 0.5, "coincident indicator claim (negative while GDP grows)")
## back-test
bta <- BT$accuracy
fam_med <- stats::aggregate(cbind(skill, skill_ic) ~ family, bta[bta$family %in% CFG$ic_families, ], median)
rownames(fam_med) <- fam_med$family
guard(all(fam_med$skill_ic > fam_med$skill), "the intercept correction should improve every ratio family's median skill")
guard(all(bta$skill_ic[bta$target == "nir_assets"] > bta$skill[bta$target == "nir_assets"]), "IC should help NIR")
guard(median(bta$skill[bta$family == "pnl"]) < 0, "fee and cost ratios should lose to no-change without the correction")
guard(median(bta$skill_used[bta$family %in% c("pricing", "credit")]) > 0, "pricing and credit should beat no-change")
## the optimiser without implied marginal costs (positioning section and What didn't work)
raw_opt <- solve_positioning(O$gradients, mv, O$weights, lambda = 4, cet1_min = CFG$cet1_min,
                             lcr_min = CFG$lcr_min, reference = NULL)
raw_gain <- sum(O$weights * (raw_opt$roe_pred - O$gradients$R0[names(O$weights)])) - raw_opt$exec_cost
raw_up <- sum(abs(raw_opt$x[1:6] - mv$upper[1:6]) < 1e-6)
guard(raw_gain > 0.01 && raw_up >= 1 && all(raw_opt$x[1:6] > 0), "raw optimiser claim")
## the audit and the further levers (summary numbers)
A0 <- rd("audit.rds"); LV0 <- rd("levers.rds")
c0r <- A0$correction; rownames(c0r) <- c0r$scenario
ns0 <- A0$nii_sens; rownames(ns0) <- c("hedged", "unhedged", "sector")
lvs0 <- LV0$summary
lv0 <- function(l, s_, col = "d_roe_weighted") lvs0[lvs0$lever == l & lvs0$setting == s_, col]
hq_set <- "A quarter of HQLA in 10-year bonds"; cmb_set <- "Ten-year reinvestment, HQLA duration and the distribution"
dist_set <- "Capital above a 12.5% CET1 returned at the jump-off"; dep_set <- "10% less of rises, 10% more of cuts"
rc0 <- LV0$ratio_curve
slope10 <- function(col) 0.1 * unname(stats::coef(stats::lm(rc0[[col]] ~ rc0$ratio))[2])   # ROE per 10 points of NMD
guard(all(abs(stats::resid(stats::lm(rc0$baseline ~ rc0$ratio))) < 1e-4), "the hedge-ratio lever is linear in the notional")
guard(slope10("baseline") > 0 && slope10("upside") > 0 && slope10("downside") < 0 && slope10("cuts") > 0,
      "summary: the hedge ratio is a rate view")
guard(all(LV0$hqla$d_roe > 0) && lv0("HQLA duration", hq_set) > 0.008 && min(LV0$hqla$d_cet1_oci_min) < -0.003,
      "summary: HQLA duration pays in every scenario, at a CET1 cost through OCI")
guard(all(LV0$levers$d_roe[LV0$levers$lever == "Reinvestment tenor" & LV0$levers$setting == "10 years"] > 0.005) &&
      LV0$pv01$vs_plan[LV0$pv01$tenor_q == 40L] > 0.5, "summary: ten-year reinvestment pays in every scenario, with more PV01")
guard(all(LV0$combo$d_roe > 0.01) && all(LV0$combo$cet1_min > CFG$cet1_min) && min(LV0$combo$cet1_min_fvoci) < CFG$cet1_min &&
      which.min(LV0$combo$cet1_min_fvoci) == which(LV0$combo$scenario == "downside"),
      "summary: the combined levers keep CET1 above the floor unless the bonds' mark-to-market runs through OCI in the downside")
guard(ns0["unhedged", "up_pct"] > A0$disclosure[["sens_bn"]] / A0$disclosure[["nii_bn"]] && ns0["hedged", "up_pct"] < 0,
      "summary: NII sensitivity against the disclosure")
## the strategy lab and the JIBAR transition (summary numbers)
LB0 <- rd("lab.rds"); lab_d0 <- LB0$dist[LB0$dist$phi == 0, ]; rownames(lab_d0) <- lab_d0$strategy
lab0 <- function(k, col) lab_d0[k, col]
lab_p10 <- sprintf("%.0f%% at 10 years", 100 * LB0$params$plan_ratio)
lab_r3 <- "R3 HQLA duration with the curve's slope"; lab_r1 <- "R1 hedge ratio with the policy rate"
lab_all <- "All seven rules"; lab_or <- "Best static hedge ratio with hindsight"
lab_as <- "25% of HQLA in asset-swapped 5-year bonds"; lab_buf <- "Buffer at an LCR of 170%"
guard(lab0(lab_p10, "win") == 1 && abs(lab0(lab_r1, "d_roe_mean")) < 0.001 &&
      lab0(lab_r3, "d_roe_mean") > lab0("25% of HQLA in 10-year bonds", "d_roe_mean") &&
      lab0("R4 payout with growth and capital", "cet1_min_fv") > lab0("Plan", "cet1_min_fv") &&
      lab0(lab_r3, "cet1_min_fv") > lab0("25% of HQLA in 10-year bonds", "cet1_min_fv") &&
      lab0(lab_as, "win") == 1 && lab0(lab_buf, "win") == 1 && abs(lab0(lab_as, "d_eve200")) < 0.005 &&
      abs(lab0(lab_buf, "d_eve200")) < 0.005 && lab0(lab_all, "cet1_min_fv") < 0.12,
      "summary: the lab's claims")
## the risk-budgeted optimiser (summary numbers)
RB0 <- rd("risk_budget.rds")
rb0v <- RB0$variants[RB0$variants$variant == "Every setting", ]
rb0r <- RB0$regime$all[RB0$regime$all$regime == "All episodes", ]
guard(RB0$carry$recommended$carry == "R50bn" && abs(RB0$carry$per_step[["roe"]] - 0.001) < 0.0002, "summary: the carry book")
guard(rb0v$win == 1 && (rb0r$as + rb0r$buf) / rb0r$total > 0.6 && (rb0r$as + rb0r$buf) / rb0r$total < 0.75 &&
      RB0$central$all[["payout"]] == "R4" && rb0v$cet1_min >= CFG$cet1_min && rb0v$eve_max <= RB0$b_central + 0.001,
      "summary: the risk-budgeted portfolio")
## the further levers that need no rate view (summary numbers)
asw0 <- LV0$asset_swap; buf0 <- LV0$buffer
guard(all(asw0$d_roe > 0.003) && max(abs(asw0$d_cet1_oci_min)) < max(abs(LV0$hqla$d_cet1_oci_min)) / 3 &&
      all(buf0$d_roe[buf0$setting == "LCR 160% at the jump-off"] > 0.006) && all(buf0$lcr_min > CFG$lcr_min),
      "summary: the asset swap and the buffer")
tr0 <- A0$transition
guard(abs(tr0$switch_effect$d_roe[1]) < 0.0005 && all(tr0$cas_risk$d_roe[tr0$cas_risk$case == "assets"] < -0.002),
      "summary: the switch is level-neutral; the spread at risk costs more than 20 bps")
## monthly frequency, share strategy and performance (summary numbers)
MM0 <- rd("monthly.rds"); DY0 <- rd("dynamics.rds"); ST0 <- rd("strategy.rds"); PF0 <- rd("performance.rds")
rr0 <- stats::reshape(MM0$race[MM0$race$block == "h1_12", c("target", "family", "model", "rmse")], idvar = c("target", "family"),
                      timevar = "model", direction = "wide")
med0m <- function(fam) stats::median((rr0[["rmse.m_ardl"]] / rr0[["rmse.q_ardl"]])[rr0$family == fam])
sg0 <- DY0$sign_check
pos0 <- ST0$positioning
pc0 <- function(p, r, col) pos0[pos0$product == p & pos0$regime == r, col]
sc0 <- PF0$scorecards
scp0 <- function(s, p) sc0$percentile[sc0$scenario == s & sc0$product == p]
cards_hd0 <- mean(ST0$margins$headroom[ST0$margins$product == "cards" & ST0$margins$scenario == "downside" &
                                         ST0$margins$funding == "wholesale"])
guard(med0m("pricing") > 1.1 && abs(med0m("volume") - 1) < 0.06, "summary: monthly does not beat quarterly")
guard(sg0$wrong_weight_free[sg0$target == "g_mortgages_res"] > 0.99, "summary: unrestricted home-loan models are wrong-signed")
guard(all(c(pc0("cards", "easing", "ngfb_effect"), pc0("corp_all", "easing", "ngfb_effect"), pc0("vaf", "easing", "ngfb_effect")) < 0) &&
      all(c(pc0("cards", "easing", "market_dev"), pc0("corp_all", "easing", "market_dev"), pc0("vaf", "easing", "market_dev")) > 0),
      "summary: easing-cycle under-participation")
guard(pc0("cards", "contraction", "action") == "Guard" && cards_hd0 > 0 && cards_hd0 < 1.5, "summary: the card guard")
guard(scp0("downside", "cards") > 0.7 && scp0("downside", "mortgages_res") < 0.5 &&
      all(vapply(c("cards", "corp_all", "vaf"), function(p) scp0("upside", p), 0) < 0.5), "summary: scorecard claims")
```

```{r blog-bridge}
#| include: false
## The complete edition carries the write-ups' explanations as well. Their numbers come from the
## write-ups' snapshot (blog/ngfb-macro-strategy/post_artefacts.rds, built by
## blog/build_post_snapshot.R from the same output/*.rds) and are evaluated in an environment of
## their own, BL, so that the write-ups' names and formatting helpers do not clash with this
## report's. Inline, B(expr) evaluates expr there; validate_post() checks the snapshot's claims.
BL <- new.env(parent = globalenv())
local({
  pdir <- file.path(root, "blog", "ngfb-macro-strategy")
  sys.source(file.path(pdir, "post_inputs.R"), envir = environment())
  S <- readRDS(file.path(pdir, "post_artefacts.rds"))
  validate_post(S)
  M <- S$meta; N <- S$ngfb
  st <- S$scen$sumtab; rownames(st) <- st$scenario
  at <- S$scen$attribution
  att <- function(s, e = "NGFB", ch = "total") at[at$scenario == s & at$entity == e, ch]
  se <- S$scen$sens; rownames(se) <- se$shock
  snh <- S$scen$sens_nohedge; rownames(snh) <- snh$shock
  wts <- S$scen$weights
  ## the bank
  bal <- N$balance; bv <- setNames(bal$balance, bal$line)
  dep_mix <- bv[c("beh_operational", "beh_notice", "beh_savings", "beh_term")]; dep_mix <- dep_mix / sum(dep_mix)
  nsh <- setNames(N$shares$share, N$shares$product)
  mix <- setNames(N$mix$ngfb, N$mix$line); mixc <- setNames(N$mix$centre, N$mix$line)
  cg <- S$stage2$coef
  drift <- function(e, p, col = "est") cg[cg$entity == e & cg$product == p & cg$param == "(Intercept)", col]
  nreg <- S$stage2$regimes
  ## positioning
  P <- S$pos; mv <- P$moves; rownames(mv) <- mv$move
  G <- P$gradients$G; cimp <- P$implied; gain <- P$gain; gni <- P$gain_ni; ps <- P$positions
  h_G <- G["downside", "hedge"]; h_c <- cimp[["hedge"]]; h_k <- mv["hedge", "cost"]
  h_x <- (h_G - h_c) / (2 * h_k)                       # points of non-maturity deposits
  bp_yr <- 1e-4 * P$m_ni[["baseline"]] / 3             # net income a year per bp of ROE (R'000)
  szp <- function(a, r, col = "gain") P$size[P$size$alpha == a & P$size$realised == r, col]
  capq <- function(cs, bs, r, col = "gain") P$capacity[P$capacity$cost_scale == cs & P$capacity$bound_scale == bs &
                                                       P$capacity$realised == r, col]
  ## share strategy and scorecards
  pb <- S$share$playbook; pbc <- function(p, r, col) pb[pb$product == p & pb$regime == r, col]
  mg <- S$share$margins; mgc <- function(p, f, col = "headroom") mg[mg$product == p & mg$funding == f, col]
  ma <- S$share$margins_all
  cards_guard <- ma$headroom[ma$scenario == "downside" & ma$product == "cards" & ma$funding == "wholesale"]
  sc <- S$share$scorecards; scc <- function(s, p, col = "percentile") sc[sc$scenario == s & sc$product == p, col]
  gn <- S$share$gainers
  gnc <- function(p, r, to) { v <- gn$share_of_loss[gn$product == p & gn$regime == r & gn$to == to]; if (length(v)) v else 0 }
  ## the audit
  A <- S$audit; pr <- A$proxy
  corr <- A$correction; rownames(corr) <- corr$scenario
  ns <- A$nii_sens; rownames(ns) <- c("hedged", "unhedged", "sector")
  tr <- A$transition; tsw <- tr$switch_effect; rownames(tsw) <- tsw$scenario
  cas <- tr$cas_risk
  jz <- A$jz; jz$basis <- 100 * (jz$jibar3m_rb - jz$zaronia)
  eb <- A$equity_breaks; eb$sarb <- exp(eb$d_sarb) - 1; eb$oecd <- exp(eb$d_oecd) - 1
  fo <- A$fund_overlay; rownames(fo) <- fo$scenario
  ## the levers
  LV <- S$levers; lvs <- LV$summary
  lv <- function(l, s, col = "d_roe_weighted") lvs[lvs$lever == l & lvs$setting == s, col]
  rc <- LV$ratio_curve
  slope10 <- function(col) 0.1 * unname(coef(lm(rc[[col]] ~ rc$ratio))[2])
  bsm <- LV$bs_model; asj <- LV$as_jo
  hq <- LV$hqla; rownames(hq) <- hq$scenario
  asw <- LV$asset_swap; rownames(asw) <- asw$scenario
  buf <- LV$buffer; bufs <- function(s, col = "d_roe", scn = "baseline") buf[buf$setting == s & buf$scenario == scn, col]
  combo <- LV$combo; rownames(combo) <- combo$scenario
  widen_max <- max(bsm$fit$bs5 - cummin(bsm$fit$bs5))   # largest rise in the spread since late 2023
  ## the strategy lab
  L <- S$lab; ld <- L$dist[L$dist$phi == 0, ]; rownames(ld) <- ld$strategy
  pl <- L$plan_by_path; info <- L$info
  plan_roe <- S$rb$plan_stats$all[["roe"]]; plan_p5 <- S$rb$plan_stats$all[["p5"]]
  drv <- setNames(L$drivers$coef, L$drivers$term)
  g3 <- merge(L$gains_r3, pl[, c("path", "d_repo_mean")], by = "path")
  r3_rise <- mean(g3$gains[g3$d_repo_mean > 0.25]); r3_fall <- mean(g3$gains[g3$d_repo_mean < -0.25])
  fr <- L$frontier; frc <- function(r, t, col) fr[abs(fr$ratio - r) < 1e-3 & fr$tenor == t, col]
  ld_n <- function(k, col) ld[k, col]
  n_up <- sum(info$repo_mean - L$params$repo_jo > 0.25); n_dn <- sum(info$repo_mean - L$params$repo_jo < -0.25)
  ## the risk-budgeted optimiser
  RB <- S$rb; cen <- RB$variants[RB$variants$variant == "Every setting", ]
  sta <- RB$variants[RB$variants$variant == "Static settings only", ]
  vr <- function(v, col = "d_roe") RB$variants[RB$variants$variant == v, col]
  rg <- RB$regime$all; rownames(rg) <- rg$regime
  rbs <- RB$scenarios; rownames(rbs) <- rbs$scenario
  fq <- RB$frontier; fqb <- function(b, st = FALSE, col = "roe") fq[abs(fq$budget - b) < 1e-9 & fq$static_only == st, col]
  spread_share <- (rg["All episodes", "as"] + rg["All episodes", "buf"]) / rg["All episodes", "total"]
  CY <- RB$carry; cyt <- CY$spread_frontier[is.finite(CY$spread_frontier$spread_step), ]
  rownames(cyt) <- cyt$carry; cyr <- CY$recommended; cyx <- RB$carry_extra
  lev_low <- pmin(cyt$lev_min, cyt$lev_scen_min); names(lev_low) <- cyt$carry
}, envir = BL)
B <- function(e) eval(substitute(e), BL)
guard(abs(B(st["baseline", "ngfb"]) - base$ngfb) < 1e-9, "the write-ups' snapshot is stale: rebuild it with blog/build_post_snapshot.R")
## light versions of the write-ups' colours, for the figure carried over
LT <- c(level = ink[["muted"]], up = pal$categorical[[1]], down = pal$diverging[["high"]], carry = pal$categorical[[4]])
```

# Summary {#summary}

**No Gut Feelings Bank (NGFB)** is a fictional South African bank, the size of
the average of the six largest banks: `r rbn(ta0)` of assets, or
`r pct(ta0 / sec_ta0)` of the BA900 sector at `r qlab(date0)`. It inherits its
deposit franchise and structural hedge from the earlier NGFB posts, takes its
asset mix from a draw on the six-bank population, and is added to the South
African banking sector so that it competes for market share with real peer
groups. This report asks four questions of it: *what does a macro scenario do
to NGFB's returns and earnings; how should the balance sheet be positioned
before the scenario arrives; where, commercially, should NGFB grow through the
cycle; and how should its performance be judged, given the macro
environment?*

Those questions are the three everyday jobs a bank's macro model can do
beyond the annual stress test: say **what to expect** from every part of the
balance sheet in each scenario, show **how to reposition** (ahead of a
scenario, with levers that need no view, and commercially against the
market), and judge **how the bank measures up** against its market and its
peers once the macro tide is taken out.
[The question and the design](#the-question-and-the-design) sets them out;
the rest of the report answers them.

The framework works top down. Macro variables are tied first to the
**banking industry** (Stage 1: `r nrow(S1$summary)` sector models of volumes,
spreads, deposit costs, credit losses, fees and costs), and only then is a
bank tied to the **industry** (Stage 2: market-share dynamics by macro regime,
pooled across banks). A quarterly engine turns the result into net interest
income, credit losses, capital, liquidity, net income and ROE; an optimiser
translates "scenario X is coming" into balance-sheet moves; and a
risk-budgeted optimiser sets the treasury levers -- the structural hedge, the
liquidity book and the payout -- together, across sixty historical macro
paths and inside limits on earnings, capital, liquidity and interest-rate
risk.

What it finds:

1. **Three scenarios.** Over the next three years NGFB's ROE averages
   `r pct(base$ngfb)` in the **baseline** (net income `r rbn(base$ni, 1)`, about
   `r rbn(base$ni / yrs, 1)` a year), `r pct(sumtab["upside", "ngfb"])` in the
   **upside** (faster disinflation and a growth dividend; `r srbn(sumtab["upside", "ni"] - base$ni)`
   of net income) and `r pct(sumtab["downside", "ngfb"])` in the **downside**
   (a stagflationary shock with SARB hikes and a two-year contraction;
   `r srbn(sumtab["downside", "ni"] - base$ni)`).
2. **NGFB earns less than the industry, and moves against it.** NGFB's
   ROE sits below the sector's (`r pct(base$sector)` in the baseline) because its
   unsecured-heavy book carries higher credit losses; its structural hedge adds
   `r ubps(base$ngfb - base$ngfb_nohedge)` in the baseline. The unhedged industry gains from higher
   rates and loses from lower ones, so its ROE barely moves in the downside
   (`r bps(att_r("downside", "Sector"))`) and falls in the upside (`r bps(att_r("upside", "Sector"))`). NGFB's hedge gives
   that rate exposure away: in the downside it loses `r ubps(att_r("downside"))`,
   `r ubps(att_r("downside", "NGFB", "credit"))` through credit losses and `r ubps(att_r("downside", "NGFB", "pricing"))` through
   pricing, because the hedge more than offsets its deposit endowment (a
   100 bps higher repo path costs hedged NGFB `r ubps(sens["repo_up_100", "total"])` of ROE and would add
   `r ubps(snh["repo_up_100", "total"])` unhedged).
3. **Credit is the largest single exposure.** GDP growth one point lower for
   three years costs `r ubps(sens["gdp_down_1", "total"])` of ROE
   (`r urm(-sens["gdp_down_1", "net_income"])` of net income), almost all through
   credit losses.
4. **Positioning before the downside** cuts the receive-fixed hedge from
   `r pct(hedge_ratio0)` to `r pct(hedge_ratio0 + posD[["hedge"]] / 100)` of
   non-maturity deposits, swaps `r pct((posD[["fund_savings"]] + posD[["fund_operational"]]) / 100, 2)`
   of assets of wholesale funding for retail deposits and trims unsecured
   lending by `r pct(-(posD[["into_cards"]] + posD[["into_personal"]]) / 100, 2)` of assets.
   It recovers `r ubps(rg$gain["downside", "downside"])` of ROE
   (`r urm(rg$gain_ni["downside", "downside"])` of net income over three years)
   if the downside comes, and costs `r ubps(rg$gain["downside", "baseline"])` if the
   baseline does and `r ubps(rg$gain["downside", "upside"])` if the upside does.
   **Before the upside** the moves reverse: extend the hedge to
   `r pct(hedge_ratio0 + posU[["hedge"]] / 100)` and lean into unsecured
   lending (`r bps(rg$gain["upside", "upside"])` if it comes).
5. **Being more aggressive moves the numbers more, in both directions.**
   Doubling the optimal moves at the same execution cost wipes out the gain
   even if the downside arrives and loses `r ubps(subset(O$aggressiveness$downside$size, alpha == 2 & realised == "upside")$gain)`
   if the upside does. A bank that can execute four times more cheaply can make
   `r ubps(subset(O$aggressiveness$downside$capacity, cost_scale == 0.25 & bound_scale == 1 & realised == "downside")$gain)`
   from the same view, but stands to lose `r ubps(subset(O$aggressiveness$downside$capacity, cost_scale == 0.25 & bound_scale == 1 & realised == "upside")$gain)`
   if it is wrong. The loss if wrong grows faster than the gain if right.
6. **The downside's key judgement is the SARB's response.** If the same
   contraction came with rate cuts (as in 2009 and 2020), the hedge would be
   NGFB's protection rather than its cost, and the optimal hedge move flips
   sign (`r sprintf("%+.1f", xc[["hedge"]])` instead of `r sprintf("%+.1f", posD[["hedge"]])`
   points of NMD); cutting unsecured lending is right in both.
7. **The hedge was priced off the wrong curve, and is corrected.** The hedge's swap
   rates came from a proxy inside the government curve that overstated actual
   ZAR swap rates by `r num(A0$proxy_err[["min"]], 1)`–`r num(A0$proxy_err[["max"]], 1)` pp, because South African bonds carry a fiscal
   premium over swaps. Priced off actual swap fixings, the hedge book's fixed
   rate falls from `r num(A0$fixed0[["proxy"]], 2)`% to `r num(A0$fixed0[["core"]], 2)`%, and NGFB's ROE by `r ubps(-c0r["baseline", "d_roe"])` in the
   baseline (`r urbn(c0r["baseline", "ni_v4"] - c0r["baseline", "ni_proxy"])` of net income over three years). Against a
   published bank's NII sensitivity (`r pct(A0$disclosure[["sens_bn"]] / A0$disclosure[["nii_bn"]])` of NII for 100 bps), unhedged NGFB
   is asset-sensitive (`r spct(ns0["unhedged", "up_pct"])` for +100 bps) and hedged NGFB liability-sensitive
   (`r spct(ns0["hedged", "up_pct"])`): its hedge is large for deposits that reprice as fast as Stage 1
   finds, and the rate-neutral ratio is `r pct(A0$neutral_ratio, 0)` of non-maturity deposits,
   not `r pct(hedge_ratio0)`. Funding spreads show no macro relationship beyond the repricing
   lag.
8. **JIBAR's cessation is now in the model, and it is level-neutral by design.**
   JIBAR is published until 31 December 2026 and new JIBAR contracts have been
   barred since 1 May 2026, so `r A0$transition$n_post` of the twelve projected quarters are priced off
   its successor: compounded ZARONIA plus the 16.19 bp fallback spread, for
   floating-rate loans, wholesale funding and the hedge's floating leg (cleared
   swaps convert to ZARONIA on 20–21 November with the spread on the floating
   leg). Because the spread is the long-run median of the JIBAR–ZARONIA basis,
   ROE moves by `r bps(A0$transition$switch_effect$d_roe[1], 1)`. What changes is risk: the basis no longer floats in a
   stress, and if borrowers negotiate the 16.19 bp away when loans are re-papered,
   NGFB loses up to `r ubps(-A0$transition$cas_risk$d_roe[A0$transition$cas_risk$scenario == "baseline" & A0$transition$cas_risk$case == "assets"])` of ROE.
9. **More levers pay than the balance-sheet mix.** Run through the engine in
   every scenario, a quarter of HQLA in ten-year government bonds adds
   `r ubps(lv0("HQLA duration", hq_set))` of probability-weighted ROE, earning the curve's fiscal term
   premium at the cost of up to `r pp(min(LV0$hqla$d_cet1_oci_min), 1)` of CET1 through OCI at the downside's peak;
   reinvesting maturing hedge tranches at ten years instead of five adds
   `r ubps(lv0("Reinvestment tenor", "10 years"))` (the swap curve's term premium, with
   `r pct(LV0$pv01$vs_plan[LV0$pv01$tenor_q == 40L], 0)` more PV01); returning capital above a 12.5% CET1 adds
   `r ubps(lv0("Distribution", dist_set))`; and passing rate rises to non-maturity deposits more slowly and cuts
   faster is worth up to `r ubps(lv0("Deposit pricing", dep_set))`, an upper bound that ignores the volume response.
   The first three together add `r ubps(lv0("Combined", cmb_set))` and keep CET1 above the floor in every
   scenario, as long as the bonds are not marked through OCI: at fair value the
   downside's peak would take CET1 to `r pct(min(LV0$combo$cet1_min_fvoci), 1)`, below the `r pct(CFG$cet1_min, 1)` floor. Two
   levers need no rate view at all: a quarter of the buffer in five-year bonds
   asset-swapped to floating collects the fiscal premium without the duration
   (`r bps(min(asw0$d_roe))` to `r bps(max(asw0$d_roe))` in every scenario, with no EVE risk and a fraction of the OCI
   risk), and releasing surplus Treasury bills to repay wholesale funding saves
   about nine basis points per R10`r nb`bn (`r bps(lv0("Liquidity buffer", "LCR 160% at the jump-off"))` at an LCR of 160%, still far above the
   floor). The hedge ratio, by contrast, is a pure rate view: each ten points
   of non-maturity deposits received fixed adds `r ubps(slope10("baseline"))` in the baseline and
   costs `r ubps(-slope10("downside"))` in the downside ([More levers](#levers)).
10. **Across sixty historical macro episodes, the term premium, the curve's
    slope and the spreads pay; timing the rate cycle does not.** Replayed from
    today's starting point, every twelve-quarter episode since 2008 gives
    NGFB's plan an average ROE of `r pct(lab0("Plan", "roe_mean"))` (5th percentile `r pct(lab0("Plan", "roe_p5"))`), and it earns its
    14.5% cost of equity in only `r sum(LB0$plan_by_path$roe >= CFG$coe)` of `r nrow(LB0$info)`. Reinvesting the hedge at ten
    years adds `r bps(lab0(lab_p10, "d_roe_mean"))` and beats the plan in every episode; holding HQLA duration
    in proportion to the government curve's slope adds `r bps(lab0(lab_r3, "d_roe_mean"))`, with a better
    capital trough than a fixed bond holding, though it gives some back through
    realised losses in hiking cycles; asset-swapped bonds (`r bps(lab0(lab_as, "d_roe_mean"))`) and a smaller
    buffer (`r bps(lab0(lab_buf, "d_roe_mean"))`) beat the plan in every episode with no rate risk; a payout
    that follows growth and capital adds a little and raises the CET1 trough; a
    hedge ratio keyed on the level of rates adds nothing, though hindsight would
    have been worth `r bps(lab0(lab_or, "d_roe_mean"))`. Seven such rules stacked together add
    `r bps(lab0(lab_all, "d_roe_mean"))`, but at `r pct(lab0(lab_all, "d_eve200"), 0)` of CET1 more EVE sensitivity to a 200 bps rise and with
    the CET1 trough at fair value down to `r pct(lab0(lab_all, "cet1_min_fv"), 2)` ([Strategy lab](#lab)).
11. **Chosen together under a risk budget, the levers add `r bps(rb0v$d_roe)` across the
    histories, with every limit met.** A risk-budgeted optimiser scores all
    `r num(RB0$n_combos, 0)` combinations of the hedge ratio and tenor, the liquidity book (ten-year
    bonds, asset swaps, the buffer's size) and the payout across the episodes,
    and keeps the best whose 5th-percentile ROE is no worse than the plan's,
    whose CET1 at fair value stays above `r pct(CFG$cet1_min, 1)`, whose LCR and NSFR stay above
    their floors and whose change in EVE for ±200 bps stays within `r pct(RB0$b_central, 0)` of CET1.
    It keeps the hedge at the rate-neutral `r RB0$central$all[["hedge_ratio"]]` reinvested at `r RB0$central$all[["hedge_tenor"]]`, puts
    `r RB0$central$all[["duration"]]` of earning HQLA in ten-year bonds and `r RB0$central$all[["asset_swap"]]` in asset-swapped bonds, cuts the buffer
    to an LCR of `r sub("LCR ", "", RB0$central$all[["buffer"]])` and pays out by R4: NGFB's average ROE rises from
    `r pct(RB0$plan_stats$all[["roe"]], 1)` to `r pct(RB0$plan_stats$all[["roe"]] + rb0v$d_roe, 1)` and it beats the plan in every episode. Two thirds of the gain is the
    two spread trades, which pay the same in every macro regime; the rest moves
    duration from swaps into bonds, so that the hedge and the bonds offset each
    other across the rate cycle. Of the macro rules only the payout rule
    survives the budget; the others are better used as risk triggers
    ([Choosing the levers together](#risk-budget)). One lever was missing: the
    balance sheet's own size. Asset-swapped government bonds funded in repo
    outside the buffer add about `r ubps(RB0$carry$per_step[["roe"]])` of ROE per R25`r nb`bn; the leverage ratio
    does not stop them, the stagflationary downside does, at `r RB0$carry$recommended$carry` (`r bps(RB0$carry$recommended$d_roe_vs_central)`),
    and they need a credit-spread limit of their own ([Using the balance sheet itself](#carry)).
12. **Is ARDL the right tool, and should it be asymmetric?** Yes, with
   asymmetries where the data support them. Judged with the macro path known
   and simulated twelve quarters ahead (perfect foresight), `r sum(MC$cw$ph < 0.10)` of `r nrow(MC$cw)`
   satellites beat an AR(1), which has no macro channel. Asymmetric pricing
   passes a fixed three-part rule for current accounts (cuts pass through
   more than rises), savings deposits, commercial mortgages and cards (yields
   lag rises and follow cuts); volumes respond symmetrically to rate rises and
   falls; card lending slows more in a contraction than growth alone predicts
   (narrowly, and only since the equity data were corrected: the kink passed
   for term deposits before); and the classic
   credit-loss kink, strongly significant in sample, fails the scenario
   back-test and stays a sensitivity. BIC-weighted model averaging beat both
   alternatives tried against it.
13. **Monthly data still do not fit better.** With the macro path known, the
    one argument for monthly data that remained -- timeliness -- disappears, and
    a scenario's GDP path is quarterly, so a monthly model would be fed a
    smooth monthly path that makes it worse still. Over twelve quarters the
    median monthly model's error is `r num(med0m("pricing"), 2)` times the quarterly in pricing and
    `r num(med0m("volume"), 2)` in volumes; credit losses and costs are slightly better monthly, not
    significantly. Production stays quarterly. The sign-restricted ARDL remains
    the best macro model at either frequency, and its sign restrictions matter
    most for volumes: left free, the home-loan model puts all of its weight on a
    *positive* response to rate hikes, because the SARB raises rates into
    credit booms.
14. **NGFB under-participates in easing cycles.** When rates fall, the card,
   corporate-loan and vehicle-finance markets grow fastest and NGFB's share of
   each falls, the card share going to the Challengers. Pushing cards pays
   even on wholesale funding; corporate lending clears the bar only narrowly
   on wholesale funding and vehicle finance barely at all, but both pay
   comfortably if they bring their own deposits. In a contraction NGFB *gains* card
   share while the market stalls, a guard case: the extra book pays only if it
   loses no more than `r num(cards_hd0, 1)` pp a year above the average card loss rate.
15. **Macro-adjusted scorecards separate the tide from the swimming.**
    Against the large-bank population, NGFB is near the frontier in cards in
    the downside (`r pct(scp0("downside", "cards"), 0)` percentile) but below par in home loans
    (`r pct(scp0("downside", "mortgages_res"), 0)`), because a typical large bank gains mortgage share in a
    contraction; in the upside it is below par in cards, corporate loans and
    vehicle finance -- exactly where the upside's growth is.

Finding 11, lever by lever: where the two points of ROE come from.

```{r headline-bridge}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 4.4
#| fig-cap: "Where two points of ROE come from. Each bar is a lever's contribution to NGFB's three-year average ROE against its plan, averaged over the replayed histories, at the central risk budget; the repo-funded carry is the lever the optimiser was missing. The two spread trades (asset-swapped bonds and the smaller buffer) need no view on rates."
with(BL, {
  ra <- rg["All episodes", ]
  wf <- data.frame(
    lab = c("Plan", "Hedge ratio\nand tenor", "Ten-year\nbonds", "Asset-\nswapped\nbonds", "Smaller\nbuffer",
            "Payout\nrule", "Inter-\naction", "Risk-\nbudgeted\nportfolio", "Repo-\nfunded\ncarry", "With the\ncarry\nbook"),
    val = 1e4 * c(0, ra$hedge, ra$dur, ra$as, ra$buf, ra$pay, ra$interaction, cen$d_roe, cyr$d_roe_vs_central, cyr$d_roe),
    kind = c("level", rep("step", 6), "level", "step", "level"))
  cum <- 0; wf$lo <- wf$hi <- NA
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(wf))) {
    if (wf$kind[i] == "level") { wf$lo[i] <- 0; wf$hi[i] <- wf$val[i]; cum <- wf$val[i] }
    else { wf$lo[i] <- cum; wf$hi[i] <- cum + wf$val[i]; cum <- cum + wf$val[i] }
  }
  wf$x <- seq_len(nrow(wf)); wf$lab <- factor(wf$lab, levels = wf$lab)
  wf$fill <- ifelse(wf$kind == "level", LT[["level"]], ifelse(wf$val >= 0, LT[["up"]], LT[["down"]]))
  wf$fill[wf$x == 9] <- LT[["carry"]]
  wf$txt <- ifelse(wf$kind == "level", sprintf("%.0f", wf$hi), sprintf("%+.0f", wf$val))
  wf$txt[1] <- sprintf("%.1f%%\nROE", 100 * plan_roe)
  ggplot(wf) +
    geom_rect(aes(xmin = x - .38, xmax = x + .38, ymin = pmin(lo, hi), ymax = pmax(lo, hi), fill = fill)) +
    geom_segment(data = wf[-nrow(wf), ], aes(x = x + .38, xend = x + .62, y = hi, yend = hi), colour = ink[["muted"]], linewidth = .3) +
    geom_text(aes(x = x, y = pmax(lo, hi) + 7, label = txt), colour = ink[["primary"]], size = 3.2, vjust = 0, lineheight = .9) +
    geom_hline(yintercept = 0, colour = ink[["secondary"]], linewidth = .3) +
    scale_fill_identity() +
    scale_x_continuous(breaks = wf$x, labels = levels(wf$lab), expand = expansion(add = .4)) +
    scale_y_continuous(limits = c(-15, 265), breaks = seq(0, 250, 50)) +
    labs(x = NULL, y = "bps of ROE against the plan") +
    theme(axis.text.x = element_text(size = 8.5, lineheight = .9), panel.grid.major.x = element_blank())
})
```

## What this complete edition adds

This edition carries everything in the v0.6.1 report and everything in the
two write-ups built from it, the long blog post *Sixty Histories and a Risk
Budget* and the short one, *The Tide and the Swimming*. Nothing in the
analysis changes; what changes is how much of it is written down.

* **Why a macro model is not just for stress tests.**
  [The question and the design](#the-question-and-the-design) now opens with
  the three everyday jobs the model does (what to expect, how to reposition,
  how the bank measures up) and maps each to the chapters that do it.
* **The engine, written out.** A new chapter, [The engine](#engine), gives net
  interest income line by line, the structural hedge's quarterly settlement,
  net income and ROE, and the switch from JIBAR to ZARONIA.
* **Every equation in plain English**: the two-stage identity, the share
  model, the random-effects pooling, the asset draw (additive log-ratios and
  the Mahalanobis truncation), the positioning problem and its closed form
  with a worked example, the headroom of new lending, the swap proxy, the
  episode regression and the EVE ratio, the risk-budget surrogate, and the
  carry book and its spread risk.
* **The system on one page**: the short post's flowchart, ahead of the
  detailed one in [The question and the design](#the-question-and-the-design).
* **Where two points of ROE come from**, lever by lever, in the
  [Summary](#summary).
* **The candidates that failed** before the carry book was found, in
  [Using the balance sheet itself](#carry).
* **An eight-point ALCO list** ([What it means for NGFB's ALCO](#alco)) and
  [Conclusions](#conclusions).
* **One table corrected**: the capital charge in the marginal-economics table
  is now grossed up to a pre-tax rate, so its columns add up to the headroom.
:::

::: {.callout-note appearance="simple"}
## What v0.6 added

* **Two more levers, in the order an ALCO sets them.** After the hedge and the
  ten-year bond book, the liquidity book now has asset-swapped government
  bonds, which collect the fiscal premium without the duration
  ([Asset-swapped bonds](#asset-swap)), and its size: surplus Treasury bills
  released to repay wholesale funding ([The size of the buffer](#buffer)). A
  [strategy map](#strategy-map) ties each lever to the macro signal that
  drives it, and the lab tests both with macro-keyed rules (R6, R7).
* **A risk-budgeted optimiser** chooses the hedge, the liquidity book and the
  payout together across the episodes, under limits on the ROE tail, CET1 at
  fair value, the LCR, the NSFR and EVE ([Choosing the levers together](#risk-budget)).
* **The bond books' accounting is explicit.** Bonds held for liquidity are at
  fair value through OCI: the unrealised mark-to-market sits in the OCI
  reserve and CET1, a sale recycles it to profit (IFRS 9), and Level 1 HQLA
  count at market value in the LCR. A rule that trades its bonds now books its
  realised gains and losses in earnings, which lowers R3's tail.
* **The bond–swap spread is modelled** from the part of the long bond's move
  the policy rate does not explain, estimated on the swap data.
* **A more detailed flowchart** of the whole chain, from data to the ALCO
  decision ([The question and the design](#the-question-and-the-design)).
* **v0.6.1 adds the lever the optimiser was missing**: repo-funded carry, the
  first lever that uses the size of the balance sheet rather than rearranging
  it, with a leverage-ratio floor, the CET1 floor checked in the named
  scenarios and a credit-spread measure ([Using the balance sheet itself](#carry)).
  The engine now reports the leverage ratio and the NSFR effect of bonds
  encumbered in repo.

The plan's own numbers do not change: NGFB's baseline ROE is `r pct(base$ngfb, 2)`, as in
the previous version (v0.5.0, 21 October 2026); every new lever is an option
against it.
:::

# The question and the design

Every quarter an ALCO gets a macro pack (the house view, an upside, a
downside, sometimes a scenario the regulator has asked for) and asks the same
three questions of it: *how exposed are we*, *what does each scenario do to our
returns*, and *what should we do before it arrives*. There is a fourth question
that rarely makes the pack, because it is uncomfortable: *what should we do
when we do not know which scenario is coming?* Which is always.

Most banks own the machinery to answer them, and point it at something else.
Macro models in a bank usually live with the stress-testing team: they turn
the regulator's adverse scenario into a capital ratio for the internal capital
adequacy assessment (ICAAP) and supply the forward-looking scenarios behind the
IFRS 9 credit provisions. Once a year they prove that the bank survives
something unpleasant, and then they go back in the cabinet with the good
crockery. That undersells them. A model that can say what a recession does to
capital can say what any macro path does to every line of the balance sheet,
which makes it useful every quarter, for three jobs a stress test never asks
of it:

* **What to expect.** What each economic outcome does to every book, margin
  and ratio, and so what the card book, the home loans or the deposit
  franchise can reasonably deliver in each scenario: the
  [scenarios](#scenarios) and the [sensitivities](#sensitivities).
* **How to reposition.** Which balance-sheet and commercial decisions depend
  on a macro view and which do not, and what each is worth either way:
  [positioning before a scenario](#positioning-before-the-scenario-arrives),
  [where NGFB should lean in](#share-strategy), the [further levers](#levers),
  the [strategy lab](#lab) and the [risk-budgeted optimiser](#risk-budget).
* **How the bank measures up.** A business that grew its book 8% while its
  market grew 12% lost ground, however well 8% presents at bonus time. Take
  the market out of each segment's growth and what is left is what management
  actually did, and how that compares with competitors:
  [macro-adjusted performance](#performance).

Answering any of them from public data needs a chain from macro variables to
a bank's balance sheet. The weak link in most attempts is the last one: a
single bank's history is short, noisy and full of idiosyncratic events
(acquisitions, strategy changes, one-off provisions, a curatorship), so
regressing a bank's metrics directly on macro variables tends to produce
elasticities that are unstable and sometimes the wrong sign. It is like
judging a flyhalf's form by the rand–dollar exchange rate: there will be a
correlation, and you will regret acting on it.

The design here estimates the macro relationships **once, on the industry**,
where they are best identified, and then models a bank **relative to the
industry**. For any product $p$ the identity

$$ g^{\text{bank}}_{p,t} = g^{\text{sector}}_{p,t} + \Delta \log s_{p,t} $$

splits a bank's growth into the sector's growth, which Stage 1 explains with
macro variables, and the change in its market share, which Stage 2 explains
with the macro *regime* and the sector cycle. The macro elasticities the bank
inherits are therefore the sector's; the bank layer only has to say whether
the bank gains or loses ground, and when.

Growth $g$ is measured in logs so that the pieces add rather than multiply,
and $s_{p,t}$ is the bank's market share of product $p$ in quarter $t$. The
first piece is how fast the whole market grew; the second is how much faster
or slower than the market the bank grew, which is exactly the change in its
market share. Being an identity, it cannot be wrong. What it does is split one
hard problem into two tractable ones: how the industry responds to the economy
is where the macro lives, and whether this bank gains or loses ground, and
when, is where the bank lives. The same split later judges performance: the
first piece is the tide and the second is the swimming.

The chain runs top to bottom. A macro path -- one of the scenarios, or one of
sixty historical episodes replayed from today -- goes through the industry
models and NGFB's share dynamics into a quarterly engine. The engine prices
NGFB's balance sheet under the levers an ALCO sets, each either fixed today
or moved by a rule that reads last quarter's macro data. Every quarter it
reports what the levers earn and the risks they take, and the optimiser
chooses the levers together inside a risk budget.

One design choice matters for everything that follows. **Nothing in this
report forecasts the economy.** Every macro path, whether a scenario or a
slice of history, is taken as given, and the only question is what it does to
the bank. That is deliberate. An ALCO will argue about which scenario is
coming whatever any model says; the model's job is to make sure everyone is
arguing about the same consequences.

On one page, the system and its three uses look like this; the detailed chain
from the data to the ALCO decision follows.

```{r system-one-page}
#| echo: false
#| fig-height: 4.1
#| fig-cap: "The system on one page. A macro path, either a scenario or a replayed slice of history, runs through the industry models and NGFB's market-share dynamics into a quarterly engine that prices the balance sheet under the levers the ALCO sets. The results serve three uses: what to expect, how to reposition, and how the bank measures up against its peers."
rbox <- function(x0, x1, y0, y1, r = .14, n = 8) {          # rounded rectangle as a polygon
  a <- seq(0, pi / 2, length.out = n)
  data.frame(x = c(x1 - r + r * cos(a), x0 + r - r * sin(a), x0 + r - r * cos(a), x1 - r + r * sin(a)),
             y = c(y1 - r + r * sin(a), y1 - r + r * cos(a), y0 + r - r * sin(a), y0 + r - r * cos(a)))
}
bx <- data.frame(rbind(
  c("macro",  0.10, 2.00, 3.60, 5.30, "THE ECONOMY",  "Macro path",         "a scenario, or a\nwindow of history\nreplayed from today", "model"),
  c("s1",     2.45, 4.35, 3.60, 5.30, "STAGE 1",      "The industry",       "volumes, margins,\nlosses, fees, costs\n(22 sector series)", "model"),
  c("s2",     4.80, 6.70, 3.60, 5.30, "STAGE 2",      "NGFB vs its market", "share gained or lost,\nby product and by\nmacro regime", "model"),
  c("eng",    7.15, 9.05, 3.60, 5.30, "ENGINE",       "The balance sheet",  "NII with the hedge,\ncredit, capital,\nliquidity, EVE", "engine"),
  c("data",   2.45, 4.35, 1.30, 2.95, "INPUT",        "Public data",        "SARB BA900, BA100,\nBA120; macro history;\nZAR swap fixings", "input"),
  c("peers",  4.80, 6.70, 1.30, 2.95, "INPUT",        "Peer population",    "six large banks,\npooled; no bank\nshown on its own", "input"),
  c("levers", 7.15, 9.05, 1.30, 2.95, "SET BY USE 2", "ALCO levers",        "hedge, bond and\nliquidity books,\npayout, lending mix", "input"),
  c("u1",     9.70, 12.0, 4.70, 6.10, "USE 1",        "What to expect",     "each scenario's effect on\nevery line, by channel", "use"),
  c("u2",     9.70, 12.0, 3.15, 4.55, "USE 2",        "How to reposition",  "positioning, levers under\na risk budget, where to\nlean in", "use"),
  c("u3",     9.70, 12.0, 1.60, 3.00, "USE 3",        "How it measures up", "growth against a macro-\nadjusted target and the\npeer range", "use")),
  stringsAsFactors = FALSE)
names(bx) <- c("id", "x0", "x1", "y0", "y1", "lab", "title", "body", "kind")
for (v in c("x0", "x1", "y0", "y1")) bx[[v]] <- as.numeric(bx[[v]])
kcol <- c(model = pal$categorical[[1]], engine = pal$categorical[[2]], input = ink[["muted"]], use = pal$categorical[[3]])
bx$col <- kcol[bx$kind]; bx$xc <- (bx$x0 + bx$x1) / 2
polys <- do.call(rbind, lapply(seq_len(nrow(bx)), function(i) cbind(rbox(bx$x0[i], bx$x1[i], bx$y0[i], bx$y1[i]), id = bx$id[i], col = bx$col[i])))
ar <- arrow(length = unit(0.07, "in"), type = "closed")
seg <- data.frame(rbind(
  c(2.00, 4.45, 2.45, 4.45), c(4.35, 4.45, 4.80, 4.45), c(6.70, 4.45, 7.15, 4.45),
  c(3.40, 2.95, 3.40, 3.60), c(5.75, 2.95, 5.75, 3.60), c(8.10, 2.95, 8.10, 3.60),
  c(9.38, 5.40, 9.70, 5.40), c(9.38, 3.85, 9.70, 3.85), c(9.38, 2.30, 9.70, 2.30)))
names(seg) <- c("x", "y", "xend", "yend")
bus <- data.frame(x = c(9.05, 9.38, 9.38), xend = c(9.38, 9.38, 9.38), y = c(4.45, 2.30, 4.45), yend = c(4.45, 5.40, 2.30))
dash <- data.frame(x = c(5.75, 5.75, 10.85), y = c(1.30, 0.95, 0.95), xend = c(5.75, 10.85, 10.85), yend = c(0.95, 0.95, 1.60))
ggplot() +
  geom_polygon(data = polys, aes(x, y, group = id), fill = "white", colour = polys$col, linewidth = .6) +
  geom_segment(data = bus, aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend), colour = ink[["secondary"]], linewidth = .4) +
  geom_segment(data = seg, aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend), colour = ink[["secondary"]], linewidth = .4, arrow = ar) +
  geom_segment(data = dash[1:2, ], aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend), colour = ink[["muted"]], linewidth = .4, linetype = "22") +
  geom_segment(data = dash[3, ], aes(x, y, xend = xend, yend = yend), colour = ink[["muted"]], linewidth = .4, linetype = "22", arrow = ar) +
  geom_path(data = data.frame(x = c(9.70, 9.22, 9.22), y = c(3.38, 3.38, 2.50)), aes(x, y), colour = ink[["muted"]], linewidth = .4, linetype = "22") +
  geom_segment(aes(x = 9.22, y = 2.50, xend = 9.05, yend = 2.50), colour = ink[["muted"]], linewidth = .4, linetype = "22", arrow = ar) +
  annotate("text", x = 0.15, y = 2.95, label = "Nothing in the chain forecasts\nthe economy. Every macro path\nis taken as given, and the\nonly question is what it\ndoes to the bank.", colour = ink[["muted"]], size = 2.5, fontface = "italic", hjust = 0, vjust = 1, lineheight = 1.05) +
  annotate("text", x = 8.3, y = 0.95, label = "par and frontier, for the scorecards", colour = ink[["muted"]], size = 2.5, vjust = 1.5) +
  annotate("text", x = 4.575, y = 5.62, label = "bank growth = market growth + change in market share", colour = ink[["muted"]], size = 2.6, fontface = "italic") +
  geom_text(data = bx, aes(xc, y1 - .2, label = lab), colour = bx$col, size = 2.3, fontface = "bold") +
  geom_text(data = bx, aes(xc, y1 - .48, label = title), colour = ink[["primary"]], size = 3.1, fontface = "bold") +

  coord_cartesian(xlim = c(0, 12.1), ylim = c(0.6, 6.2), expand = FALSE) +
  theme_void() + theme(plot.background = element_rect(fill = "#fcfcfb", colour = NA))
```

| Strategy lab | `pnl_engine.R` (hedge paths, payout rules, overlays, buffer), `treasury.R` (bond books) | `analysis/lab_tools.R`, `analysis/14_strategy_lab.R` | `lab.rds` |
| Risk-budgeted optimiser | the same | `analysis/lab_tools.R`, `analysis/15_risk_budget.R` | `risk_budget.rds` |

: Pipeline. Every number in this report is read from the `output/*.rds` files and checked with `guard()` before it is printed. {.striped}

# Data

```{r data-coverage}
#| echo: false
man <- P$manifest
b9 <- man[man$form == "BA900", ]
rc <- P$reconcile
rc_max <- max(abs(c(rc$asset_gap, rc$le_gap)), na.rm = TRUE)
guard(rc_max < 1e-4, "BA900 reconciliation gap %.2e", rc_max)
dm <- P$depmat
mem <- stats::aggregate(members ~ entity, P$membership, function(x) c(min = min(x), max = max(x)))
mem <- data.frame(entity = mem$entity, min = mem$members[, "min"], max = mem$members[, "max"])
guard(all(mem$min >= ngfb_canonical()$k_anon), "k-anonymity breached")
macro_last <- max(P$macro$date[is.finite(P$macro$gdp_yy)])
ros <- P$roster
oth <- ros[ros$group == "Other", ]
oth_n <- vapply(sort(unique(P$gp$date[P$gp$entity == "Other"])), function(d) sum(oth$first <= d & oth$last >= d), 0)
guard(min(oth_n) >= ngfb_canonical()$k_anon, "the residual group is too small")
```

Everything is public. The SARB's BA returns come through its web API
(`custom.resbank.co.za/SarbWebApi`), with the existing pull harness in this
project; macro series come from the SARB's key-indicator releases and from FRED.

| Source | What it gives | Coverage used |
|---|---|---|
| **BA900** (economic return), per bank | balance sheet by product and counterparty; deposits by depositor and contractual bucket | `r b9$periods` periods, `r format(as.Date(b9$first), "%b %Y")` to `r format(month_start(b9$last), "%b %Y")`; `r b9$institutions` institutions including the sector total |
| **BA100 / BA120** (sector only) | balance sheet and income statement: interest by product, fees, costs, impairments, tax | monthly to `r format(as.Date(man$last[man$form == "BA120"]), "%b %Y")` |
| **BA200 / BA700** (sector only) | credit risk-weighted exposure by asset class; capital adequacy, RWA, CET1 | to `r format(as.Date(man$last[man$form == "BA700"]), "%b %Y")` |
| SARB key indicators | repo, prime, long bond yield, CPI, rand, JSE All Share, business-cycle indicators, private credit | to `r qlab(max(P$macro$date[is.finite(P$macro$repo)]))` |
| FRED (OECD, BIS, Stats SA via FRED) | real GDP, unemployment, house prices, 3-month JIBAR, 10-year yield, household debt | real GDP to `r qlab(macro_last)` |
| Prudential Authority, *Selected South African banking sector trends* (June 2025) | sector LCR 149.59%, NSFR 117.29%, CET1 13.25% | calibration targets |
| rbond.co.za (CC BY 4.0) | daily JIBAR interest-rate swap fixings (SASW, 1, 2, 3, 5 and 10 years; floating leg 3-month JIBAR), 3-month JIBAR, ZARONIA, the repo rate, FRA and generic government yields (3, 5 and 10 years) | swaps from September 2023, government yields from September 2018, to October 2026 |
| SARB Market Practitioners Group; CME Group | JIBAR cessation: last fixing 31 December 2026, no new JIBAR contracts from 1 May 2026, fallback to compounded ZARONIA plus 16.19 bp; clearing-house conversion of JIBAR swaps (20–21 November 2026) | the floating benchmark from 2027Q1 |
| SARB Monetary Policy Committee statements | repo at 7.00% after May 2026 and 7.25% after 24 September 2026; inflation above 5% around the turn of the year, back at the 3% target by late 2027 | baseline policy and inflation path |

: Data sources. {.striped}

Three properties of the data shape everything that follows.

* **Only BA900 is published per bank.** Income statements, capital and
  liquidity exist only for the sector (BA1xx, BA200, BA700). This is the
  practical reason for the two-stage design: bank-level information is
  balance-sheet volumes; prices, losses and costs are sector-level.
* **The sector returns end in June 2025; BA900 runs to mid-2026.** Sector
  margins and losses are therefore projected through the four missing
  quarters along the realised macro path before any scenario starts, which is
  the models' job: the macro data are known, the banking outcomes are not.
* **Real banks are only ever shown pooled.** Every peer group has at least
  `r min(mem$min)` members in every quarter (k-anonymity of at least four), and
  the six large banks enter NGFB only through population hyperparameters and
  pooled averages.

BA900 is internally consistent: across all banks and periods the product lines
reproduce reported total assets and total liabilities to within
`r formatC(rc_max, format = "e", digits = 1)` (relative). The depositor-by-bucket
deposit matrix used for the liquidity proxies adds up exactly to the
behavioural deposit lines.

## Who is in each peer group

```{r peer-groups}
#| echo: false
prof <- peer_group_profiles()
named <- ros[ros$group != "Other", ]
span <- do.call(rbind, lapply(split(named, named$key), function(z) data.frame(
  key = z$key[1], group = z$group[1], first = min(z$first), last = max(z$last),
  names = paste(unique(tools::toTitleCase(tolower(z$name))), collapse = "; "), stringsAsFactors = FALSE)))
span$bank <- prof$bank[match(span$key, prof$key)]
span$description <- prof$description[match(span$key, prof$key)]
span$in_data <- ifelse(span$last >= date0 & span$first <= as.Date("2008-03-31"), "throughout",
                       paste(qlab(span$first), "to", qlab(span$last)))
span <- span[order(match(span$group, c("Big Four", "Challengers", "Specialists")), span$first, span$bank), ]

kt(data.frame(Group = span$group, Bank = span$bank, `In the BA900 data` = span$in_data,
              `Who they are` = span$description, check.names = FALSE),
   align = "llll", caption = sprintf("Named banks by peer group. Members per quarter: Big Four %d to %d, Challengers %d to %d, Specialists %d to %d. Corporate history as publicly reported (see the sources at the end). Membership only: no result in this report is shown for an individual bank.",
     mem$min[mem$entity == "Big Four"], mem$max[mem$entity == "Big Four"],
```

The grouping follows business model and growth path rather than size alone.
The **Big Four** are the universal banks that have dominated South African
banking for decades. The **Challengers** are the retail and digital banks that
have taken market share from them since 2008, Capitec above all; Capitec is
now the largest retail bank by number of clients, but its balance sheet,
funding and growth pattern are a challenger's, so it is grouped there. The
**Specialists** are niche business, private-client, Islamic and
community banks. Imperial Bank is counted with the Big Four because Nedbank
owned it and its book continued inside Nedbank (the pro-forma treatment
keeps the group's history free of an artificial jump in 2010).

# NGFB: the bank

## What is canonical, and what is new

```{r canon}
#| echo: false
cn <- ngfb_canonical()
B0 <- stats::setNames(bal$balance, bal$line)
iea0 <- sum(B0[setdiff(ngfb_asset_lines(), "other_assets")])
dep0 <- sum(B0[c("beh_operational", "beh_notice", "beh_savings", "beh_term")])
guard(abs(iea0 / B0[["equity"]] - cn$leverage_iea_equity) < 1e-8, "NGFB leverage is not canonical")
guard(abs(dep0 / iea0 - cn$all_dep_iea) < 1e-8, "NGFB deposit ratio is not canonical")
guard(all(abs(B0[names(cn$deposit_mix)] / dep0 - cn$deposit_mix) < 1e-10), "NGFB deposit mix is not canonical")
```

NGFB carries over everything the earlier posts fixed, and extends the bank to a
full balance sheet with the same rule the deposit posts used: a typical large
South African bank drawn from the population, never a copy of any one of them.

| Item | Value | Origin |
|---|---|---|
| Seed | `r cn$seed` | Post 1 |
| Deposit mix: operational / notice / savings / term | `r paste(pct(cn$deposit_mix[c("beh_operational", "beh_notice", "beh_savings", "beh_term")]), collapse = " / ")` | Post 1 canonical draw (`ngfb_composition_canonical.csv`) |
| Deposit betas (one-month slopes) | `r paste(num(cn$deposit_beta[c("beh_operational", "beh_notice", "beh_savings", "beh_term")], 3), collapse = " / ")` | Post 1 |
| Interest-earning assets / equity | `r num(cn$leverage_iea_equity, 2)` | Post 3 BA100 bridge |
| All deposits / interest-earning assets | `r num(cn$all_dep_iea, 3)` | Post 3 BA100 bridge |
| Structural hedge | `r pct(cn$hedge_ratio)` of NMD, receive-fixed, 5-year rolling boxcar at an average fixed rate of `r num(SC$hedge0$fixed0, 2)`% (actual ZAR swap rates) | Post 3 optimum |
| Size | mean total assets of the six large banks: `r rbn(ta0)` | new |
| Asset composition | business-line draw from the six-bank population | new |
| Other funding | the population's mix of repo, wholesale and other liabilities | new |

: NGFB's identity. The deposit block, leverage and hedge are checked against the canonical constants before anything is computed. {.striped}

::: {.callout-warning appearance="simple"}
## A note on Post 2's weights
Post 2 loaded `post1_betas.rds`, whose weights (23.9 / 8.9 / 23.4 / 43.7) are
an older draw. The canonical composition is the one Post 1 published and Post 4
used (41.7 / 10.8 / 7.5 / 39.9), and that is what NGFB carries here.
:::

## The asset draw

```{r asset-draw}
#| fig-height: 3.2
#| fig-cap: "NGFB's business-line mix against the population centre. The draw lands on the unsecured-heavy side of the six banks: inside the truncation radius, but more than twice the centre's unsecured share."
ad <- N$asset_draw
bl_lab <- c(retail_secured = "Retail secured", retail_unsecured = "Retail unsecured",
            corporate = "Corporate", treasury = "Treasury", hqla = "HQLA", other = "Other assets")
dd <- data.frame(line = factor(bl_lab[names(ad$line_draw)], levels = rev(bl_lab)),
                 NGFB = as.numeric(ad$line_draw), centre = as.numeric(ad$line_mean[names(ad$line_draw)]))
guard(abs(sum(dd$NGFB) - 1) < 1e-10 && abs(sum(dd$centre) - 1) < 1e-10, "composition shares do not sum to one")
dl <- rbind(data.frame(line = dd$line, who = "NGFB", share = dd$NGFB),
            data.frame(line = dd$line, who = "Population centre", share = dd$centre))
ggplot(dd, aes(y = line)) +
  geom_segment(aes(x = centre, xend = NGFB, yend = line), colour = ink[["axis"]], linewidth = 0.6) +
  geom_point(data = dl, aes(x = share, colour = who), size = 3) +
  scale_colour_manual(values = c(NGFB = ent_col[["NGFB"]], `Population centre` = ink[["muted"]])) +
  scale_x_continuous(labels = scales::percent_format(1), limits = c(0, NA)) +
  labs(x = "share of total assets", y = NULL)
```

```{r asset-draw-twin}
#| echo: false
#| results: asis
twin(data.frame(`Business line` = as.character(dd$line), NGFB = pct(dd$NGFB), `Population centre` = pct(dd$centre),
                check.names = FALSE))
```

Balance-sheet shares are awkward objects to draw. They are positive and they
add up to one, so a normal distribution cannot be put on them directly: a
normal draw would happily produce negative mortgages. The standard fix is the
additive log-ratio transform (Aitchison 1986). Divide every share $w_k$ by a
reference share $w_K$ and take logs,

$$z_k \;=\; \log\frac{w_k}{w_K}, \qquad k = 1,\dots,K-1,$$

which turns $K$ shares that must add to one into $K-1$ unconstrained numbers.
Fit a multivariate normal to the banks' $z$'s, draw from it, and transform
back: every draw is then a valid balance sheet, and the shares follow a
logistic-normal distribution. The draw is truncated by its Mahalanobis
distance from the population centre,

$$d \;=\; \sqrt{(z-\mu)^{\top}\,\Sigma^{-1}\,(z-\mu)} \;\le\; r ,$$

which measures how far a draw sits from the centre in units that allow for
the spread and correlation of the population: in one dimension, $d = 1$ is
one standard deviation.

Six banks cannot identify an eleven-dimensional covariance of product shares,
so the draw is made over six business lines (five dimensions in additive
log-ratio space) from a logistic-normal fitted to the six banks' average
compositions over the last eight quarters, and products are split within each
line at the population's average within-line mix. The draw is truncated to
the same central probability mass as Post 1's composition draw (radius 1 in
three dimensions keeps the central `r pct(pchisq(1, 3))`; the equivalent radius
in five dimensions is `r num(ad$radius, 2)`). NGFB's draw sits at Mahalanobis
distance `r num(ad$distance, 2)`.

The seed puts NGFB on the unsecured side of the population: retail unsecured
lending is `r pct(ad$line_draw[["retail_unsecured"]])` of assets against the
centre's `r pct(ad$line_mean[["retail_unsecured"]])`. That is a legitimate member
of the population (one of the six is an unsecured specialist), and it is kept
because the seed is canonical, but it colours every result: NGFB's credit-loss
ratio is higher than the sector's, and it is more exposed to the credit cycle.

```{r balance-sheet}

              vaf = "Vehicle and asset finance", cards = "Credit cards", personal_other = "Personal and other retail",
              corporate_loans = "Corporate loans", overdrafts = "Overdrafts", interbank = "Interbank",
              reverse_repo = "Reverse repo", hqla = "HQLA (cash, central bank, government)",
              other_securities = "Other securities", other_assets = "Other assets",
              beh_operational = "Operational deposits", beh_notice = "Notice deposits",
              beh_savings = "Savings deposits", beh_term = "Term deposits", repo_funding = "Repo funding",
              wholesale_other = "Wholesale and other funding", other_liabilities = "Other liabilities",
              equity = "Equity")
sbs <- SC$sector_bs; sbs_ta <- sum(sbs$balance[sbs$side == "asset"])
bt <- merge(bal[, c("line", "side", "balance")], sbs[, c("line", "balance")], by = "line", suffixes = c("", "_sec"), sort = FALSE)
bt <- bt[match(bal$line, bt$line), ]
guard(abs(sum(bt$balance_sec[bt$side == "asset"]) / sec_ta0 - 1) < 1e-8, "sector balance sheet does not tie to BA900 total assets")
kt(data.frame(Line = lab_line[bt$line], Side = ifelse(bt$side == "asset", "asset", ifelse(bt$side == "equity", "equity", "funding")),
              `NGFB, R bn` = num(bt$balance / 1e6, 0), `NGFB, % of assets` = pct(bt$balance / ta0),
```
